how: The first tiny flag is retrospectively attributed to a named maker, separately from subsequent recruitment and organizing
Calls repeatedly solicit flag construction, growth and repair while separate calls recruit for memorial and other causes
Brief direct replies accept a tile-order instruction and offer help with a border
Questions elicit explanations of timed placement, the closed event and its alliances in ordinary and Irish-language venues
Participants oppose a war for lack of manpower and shrink an emblem for lack of room
Criticism of a drawing proposal elicits a rebuke and personal exchanges rather than remaining practical design discussion
Members repeatedly revise proportions, lettering and emblems rather than follow a single settled design
Members report a temporarily completed tricolour and its continuing state
Coordinates locate the shared flag and its outline is credited with aligning contributors
Repair scripts multiply placements while members dispute their value and stop outdated versions
Maintenance restores an earlier form against intended progress until incompatible scripts are stopped or updated
Participants invite helpers to chat to avoid conflicting work and relay diplomatic instructions back to the thread
Participants describe addiction, defensive labour across venues and fitting placing into work and overnight availability
Participants test apparent extra placements across tabs and an incognito window rather than assuming displayed edits persisted
Members acknowledge friendly mistakes, suggest outside placers and correct a mistaken attack attribution
An appointed ambassador returns from neighbouring groups with a defence plan
Participants negotiate designs and borders while invoking or contesting agreements with neighbours
Members invoke an understanding to spare neighbouring work and apologize for mistakenly damaging an ally
Assistance is requested, offered conditionally, refused or exchanged for keeping shared territory intact
Participants report a common defence plan and conditional cooperation against a shared threat
Other groups keep artwork on the flag while participants vet requests and contest who owns the space
Participants state that chat members lack authority to commit all placers and distinguish coordinating venues from wider activity
Participants propose a corner, expand away from a threat and scale down an emblem before any demonstrated rebuilding after erasure
Complaints about covering and broken agreements receive arguments for reciprocal tolerance and earlier occupants having greater entitlement
Existing national identity, colour allegiance and local lore furnish imagery and arguments for canvas action
Republican and national identifications enact inherited antagonism against the Union Jack without documenting an earlier interforum dispute
Republican identification names the Union Jack in the same turn inviting slogans over it
Canvas details generate checkpoint, lettering and lime-white-and-lemon wordplay
Participants object to divisive sectarian lettering and endorse an inclusive substitute without demonstrating rejection of every insult
A false Vatican story is explicitly recognized as an April Fools joke rather than evidence that every attack call is joking
Removal rules and specialist venues contain canvas discussion while participants contest enforcement and the activity's worth
Members celebrate the work and add recognition of night defenders to collective credit
Members request final images, supply links, mourn losses and photograph a figure when screenshots fail
Members commemorate the weekend in a banner and propose continued music, gifts and games with former neighbours
Members correct a memorial copy and challenge retrospective claims about invasion and friendship
Allied work brings visitors who receive hospitality and invitations into ordinary game contact without a demonstrated subscriber count
Members recruit flag overwriting and later recount both encroachment and restoration
A participant continues the wall contest in talk by contrasting the surviving heart with the vanished wall
A participant retrospectively explains mobilization as discovering an already begun flag, without directly documenting the initial call chain
A temporarily completed flag becomes work to defend even as further additions remain planned
A reply invokes an understanding and prior occupancy as reasons to stop treating neighbouring work as an invasion
A report that the flag looks well elicits praise directed at the builders and their efficiency
A cleaned image supplies an object to frame while a reused banner commemorates the weekend
A participant explicitly describes background territory being exchanged for neighbours keeping the flag and art intact
A call to take a corner receives calls to block and overwrite the British flag
Attack proposals receive neutrality and friendship-based refusals in their own threads
A call against neighbouring builders is answered by invoking an existing understanding instead
Participants describe a joint defence plan and offer conditional protection against a shared threat
Complaints about constant canvas calls and scattered updates elicit megathread redirection and disputes over removal enforcement
Written joining and self-reported recruitment support participation but do not trace every call through actual placements and construction reports
Defensive negotiations address a shared external threat rather than demonstrating that the negotiating neighbours themselves eroded the flag
A developer explicitly connects a script to vandalism repair without establishing that interval-limited manpower necessarily forced adoption
Posting a revised design cannot settle implementation while active scripts still restore incompatible targets
Direct bare acceptances are observable but neither silent placement nor every reader's response obligations are established
A claim to host artwork must accommodate earlier occupants whose work the expanding background engulfed
Permission to add artwork depends on acceptable national representation rather than unrestricted hospitality
Rebukes can be followed by sustained reciprocal taunts and renewed contact rather than reconciliation or departure
Maintenance is followed by further construction tasks, so keeping the work does not end design and building once and for all
An agreed border design cannot be carried out until maintaining scripts are changed to permit it
National representational judgments qualify whose art may be hosted, including refusing a stereotyped addition
One room cannot test global prevalence, while its designation, sanction and thread control identify explicit local organization
Siting, scaling and expansion proposals do not establish moving to a new spot after erasure
A warning about inadequate manpower opposes further attack without demonstrating abandonment and relocation caused by shortage
Closing thanks and final-image requests coexist without establishing that celebration caused preservation
Proposing an allied help request under attack does not establish the complete shortage, request and delivered assistance chain
The immediate antecedent of a post-event rivalry taunt is an art-class insult rather than a demonstrated canvas attack
Authority disclaimers and complaints about good terms do not identify specific agreed terms followed by refusal or a later compliance disclaimer
A pointer to a specialist strategy venue and invitations to an existing colour group do not establish founding a new faction around a mark
Plans for a gallery print and a framed copy do not establish outreach to represented creators, staff or the press
An existing Irish-language weekly thread provides explanation without establishing covert strategy or infiltration
Reporting surplus posts and calling the activity juvenile do not establish sabotaging the flag because its posts are annoying
Working between two communities and thanking an ally do not explicitly establish dual membership or a divided-loyalty dilemma
